args.title: Reject non-numeric TTL environment values instead of silently truncating
args.body:
File: src/config.ts

The int() helper uses Number.parseInt, which happily reads "12h" as 12 instead of failing. Change it to reject any value that isn't a plain integer string (e.g. via Number.isInteger(Number(raw)) or a strict regex) so a typo like TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES=12h or RESET_TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES=1h stops the service at startup with a clear error, rather than being silently misread as minutes.

args.title: Honor Accept-Language q weights when picking a locale
args.body:
File: src/i18n/index.ts

pickLocale() takes the first supported language token in the header, ignoring the ;q= weights, so "en;q=0.3, fr-FR;q=0.9" resolves to English. Parse and sort by q value (defaulting to 1 when absent) before picking the first supported locale, so a header like this one correctly resolves to fr.

args.body:
label: bug
file: src/config.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The config loader's int() helper uses Number.parseInt, which reads "12h" as 12 and "1h" as 1 instead of rejecting the value, so a unit-suffixed TTL is silently misread as minutes rather than failing fast at startup. Tightening that parser to reject anything but a plain integer string fixes both TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES and RESET_TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES.

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

This is working as documented: docs/API.md already states that /health returns 503 only when the database is down. src/api/health.ts treats "degraded" (queue backlog over 500 jobs) as still able to serve traffic, so it intentionally returns 200 with status: "degraded" in the body. Point your probe at the HTTP status code for pass/fail (503 = take out of rotation), and alert separately on the JSON "status"/"checks.queue" fields for degraded, rather than tying rotation to "degraded".

file: src/i18n/index.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

pickLocale() walks the Accept-Language header in list order and returns the first supported language, ignoring the ;q= weights entirely, so "en;q=0.3, fr-FR;q=0.9" resolves to English even though French is preferred. It should parse each part's q value (default 1) and pick the supported locale with the highest weight.
